chunks: 5237 - It was reported to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام:

Three men: one of them restrained a man, another came and killed him, and the third was watching them. So he, عليه السلام, ruled regarding the watcher that his eyes be gouged out; and he ruled regarding the one who restrained [the victim] that he be imprisoned until he dies, just as he held him; and he ruled regarding the one who killed that he be killed.

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: The Commander of the Faithful, Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام
key_terms.تُسْمَلَ عَيْنَاهُ: His eyes are to be gouged out
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الرُّؤْيَةِ: The one who witnessed the act while watching
key_terms.يُسْجَنَ حَتَّى يَمُوتَ: He is to be imprisoned until death

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling of Imam Ali عليه السلام on those who participated in a murder in different ways?
ai.summary: This hadith records a judicial ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning three different levels of participation in a murder. It assigns distinct punishments to the killer, the one who physically restrained the victim, and the one who knowingly stood by watching, showing graded legal liability in violent crime.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5237 - It was reported to the Commander of the Faithful (as) about three men: one of them restrained a man, another approached and killed him, and the third stood by watching them.
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ruled that the one who merely watched should have his eyes gouged out. Imam (as) ruled that the one who restrained the victim should be imprisoned until he dies, just as he held the victim until death. As for the one who committed the murder, Imam (as) ruled that he should be executed.
